And I want to congratulate them all. They worked so hard and uh they did a really terrific job. So, uh we're going to do something we've never done before here at a Macworld. Uh I get to tell you uh what our revenues were for last quarter. It was Apple's uh a record for Apple, the highest revenues we've ever had in a quarter. Last quarter we sold around $5.7 billion.

So, this is uh one for the record books. So, there's a lot for these ginger mint gingerbread men to be uh dancing about. Everybody's pretty happy. So, that's a retail update. And uh now what I'd like to do is talk about our efforts in music. We went into the holiday quarter with the best lineup of music players on the planet. Uh the new iPod Nano and the fifth generation iPod. These are the best music players in the world and of course the fifth generation iPod also plays video, music videos and now television shows as well. And we sold 4 and a half million iPods a year ago in the holiday quarter 2004. And what a lot of folks have been asking us and speculating on is how many did we sell last quarter? Holiday quarter 2005 and some of the estimates were getting pretty astronomical. 8 million, 9 million, 10 million. Uh and I'm really pleased to announce today uh that last quarter we sold 14 million iPods.

That is over 100 every minute 24/7 throughout the whole quarter. And it's still it still wasn't enough. So uh more iPods are on their way for those people that uh didn't have a chance to get one last quarter. And so that brings the total number of iPods sold to around 42 million. Uh you can see the slope of this curve is going up again. And of those 42 million, 32 million of them were sold in 2005, in calendar year 2005. 32 million iPods. Okay. **[Audience]**: [Applause]

**[Steve Jobs]**: Good morning and welcome to Macworld. We've got a lot of great stuff for you today.

**[Audience]**: [Applause]

**[Steve Jobs]**: So, I want to start off with a retail update. Tell you how we did in Apple retail stores. You know, we've got 135 Apple retail stores now. And these are just the best place to buy not only a Mac and an iPod, but one of the best buying experiences for any product in the world. And I am really pleased to announce that last quarter we had 26 million visitors during the holiday quarter in our retail stores. I mean, think about it. This is more people than live in any state in our union but California. You know, if you're in New Hampshire, it's no big deal, but if you live in New York, I mean, everybody in New York visited an Apple store by number, you know, it's it's incredible. So, that was pretty amazing. What was also amazing was that our retail stores had their first billion dollar quarter. Over a billion dollars of revenues last quarter. So, really fantastic. And I want to congratulate them all. They worked so hard and uh they did a really terrific job. Now, uh we've got a great chief financial officer, Peter Oppenheimer, and Peter told me that if I wanted to release uh this figure, I also had to release the overall sales for Apple because he didn't want anybody making the wrong assumptions and and uh and and getting the wrong data for the quarter. So, uh we're going to do something we've never done before here at a Macworld. Uh I get to tell you uh what our revenues were for last quarter. It was Apple's uh a record for Apple, the highest revenues we've ever had in a quarter. Last quarter we sold around $5.7 billion.

**[Audience]**: [Applause]

**[Steve Jobs]**: So, this is uh one for the record books. So, there's a lot for these ginger mint gingerbread men to be uh dancing about. Everybody's pretty happy. So, that's a retail update. And uh now what I'd like to do is talk about our efforts in music. We went into the holiday quarter with the best lineup of music players on the planet. Uh the new iPod Nano and the fifth generation iPod. These are the best music players in the world and of course the fifth generation iPod also plays video, music videos and now television shows as well. And we sold 4 and a half million iPods a year ago in the holiday quarter 2004. And what a lot of folks have been asking us and speculating on is how many did we sell last quarter? Holiday quarter 2005 and some of the estimates were getting pretty astronomical. 8 million, 9 million, 10 million. Uh and I'm really pleased to announce today uh that last quarter we sold 14 million iPods.

**[Audience]**: [Applause]

**[Steve Jobs]**: That is over 100 every minute 24/7 throughout the whole quarter. And it's still it still wasn't enough. So uh more iPods are on their way for those people that uh didn't have a chance to get one last quarter. And so that brings the total number of iPods sold to around 42 million. Uh you can see the slope of this curve is going up again. And of those 42 million, 32 million of them were sold in 2005, in calendar year 2005. 32 million iPods. Okay. Now, I'd like to give you an update on iTunes. We have sold on iTunes. We've crossed over 850 million songs. We are well on our way to hitting that billion song mark in the next few months. And we are selling songs at the rate now of 3 million per day. We've seen a really nice growth in iTunes sales. And that is over a billion songs a year run rate. Well over. So, we've seen some really great growth throughout the last year in iTunes as well. And our market share continues to be very strong. 83%.

**[Audience]**: [Applause]

**[Steve Jobs]**: Yeah, I'm showing off some new keynote features here too. Couldn't help myself. So, we're really, really happy uh with how iTunes is doing. And as you know, one of the newest things in iTunes and of course on iPod are television shows and the content that we've been adding has just been spectacular. And we started selling TV shows only about 90 days ago. I'm very pleased to report uh that since we launched on October 12th, we have sold over 8 million videos. We are really happy with this. Now, last week last week for the first time we added some sports. And in partnership with ABC and ESPN, we put up the bowl games and it was really fantastic. Here's a little sampling.

**[Speaker 2]**: Hello everybody and welcome to Pasadena, California. Night of the 2006 Rose Bowl game presented by City. I'm Keith Jackson and in the unprecedented partnership between ABC Sports and Apple iTunes, you're about to see a bowl blast. The 15 minute condensed version of the National Championship game between the top ranked USC Trojans and the number two Texas Longhorns. All the key moments from this contest right at your fingertips in the iTunes video store. And it's available for all four BCS games. So, sit back, relax and enjoy this special ABC Sports presentation.

**[Audience]**: [Applause]

**[Steve Jobs]**: So, uh ABC and ESPN did a phenomenal job on these 15 minute highlights and they they went to number one. The Rose Bowl is the number one video now on iTunes. So they've been extremely popular. And today we're putting up some other great new content from Saturday Night Live. This is this is some stuff that I've personally wanted to see from day one.
